subject.title: fix(discord): disable ws 8.21.0 receiver part limits for gateway sockets

question: Should OpenClaw disable ws 8.21 retained-part caps for trusted Discord gateway sockets while relying on the 16 MiB `maxPayload` cap, or require finite retained-part caps instead?
rationale: The code path and dependency contract support the mitigation, but accepting unlimited fragment/chunk counts is a security and availability boundary decision that automation should not make for maintainers.

options.title: Accept Discord-only disablement
options.body: Land this PR if maintainers agree Discord gateway is a trusted peer and `maxPayload` is the right remaining resource bound.

options.title: Require finite retained-part caps
options.body: Ask for calibrated nonzero `maxBufferedChunks` and `maxFragments` values plus proof that large real Discord gateway events still pass.

options.title: Reject this mitigation
options.body: Close or replace the PR if maintainers prefer pinning/downgrading ws or waiting for upstream behavior instead of changing OpenClaw socket options.

recommendation.title: Accept Discord-only disablement
recommendation.body: Land this PR if maintainers agree Discord gateway is a trusted peer and `maxPayload` is the right remaining resource bound.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned to the PR and authored the recent ws gateway transport and diagnostic commits around this exact failure mode.
